key_insight: TDFold reframes 3D protein structure prediction as a 2D image-like diffusion task: it diffuses and denoises geometric template maps (pairwise geometry) to produce accurate 3D structures from a single sequence.
problem_solved: Reduces reliance on expensive MSAs and heavy 3D diffusion pipelines by enabling fast, accurate single-sequence protein structure prediction with lower compute and latency.
method: Encode 3D geometry as 2D geometric templates (pairwise distance/orientation maps) that resemble image channels.
Train a diffusion model to denoise and refine these 2D templates, producing high-quality geometric restraints.
Efficiently decode the refined 2D templates into 3D coordinates, achieving improved accuracy, speed, and resource efficiency versus leading models.
impact: Makes high-quality structure prediction accessible in low-resource or high-throughput settings and demonstrates how diffusion models + geometric inductive bias can replace heavier MSA/3D approaches—relevant for ML practitioners building efficient scientific models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: single-sequence → 2D geometric templates → diffusion denoising → 3D coordinate decode.
Side-by-side comparison chart: accuracy and runtime of TDFold vs MSA-based and 3D diffusion baselines.
Illustration of a 2D pairwise geometry map (heatmap + orientation channels) showing how it corresponds to a 3D fold.
Icon set: single-sequence input, lightning bolt for speed, chip for low compute, and accuracy target.
paper_title: Two-dimensional geometric template diffusion for boosting single-sequence protein structure prediction
paper_authors: Xudong Wang, Tong Zhang, Zhen Cui, Xu Guo, Fuyun Wang
